reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004101C0 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/define/004101C0-DefineHumanPlayerWeaponCycle.cpp at sha256 75339913402f03ef39e8b2d8d8bbd8d884f8eba6cb1076246522e897d1e42565 (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t DefineHumanPlayerWeaponCycle(int32_t param_1, int32_t* param_2);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: DefineHumanPlayerWeaponCycle
retail_function.summary: Three blocks 0x4101C0-0x410216: g_weapon_cycle_count=0; if (*frame>0) loop i<*frame: table[count]=Script_EvalArgInt(frame,i); count++; return 1.

candidate_function.summary: Three blocks 0x4101C0-0x410216: g_weapon_cycle_count=0; if (*frame>0) loop i<*frame: table[count]=Script_EvalArgInt(frame,i); count++; return 1.

divergences: Frame pointer read from [E+8] instead of [E+0xc].
Loop bound and Script_EvalArgInt use the argc word.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: BN int32_t(int32_t arg1, int32_t* arg2 @ 0xc): the frame is the third word. The candidate (int32_t param_1, int32_t* param_2) puts param_2 at [E+8].The retail frame slot is [E+0xc] (BN already models it as arg2/arg3 with an explicit @ 0xc offset). The candidate declaration puts its second (or third) parameter at [E+8], the registered argc slot, so the same source compiled into the QVM call site would read the wrong stack word.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1, int32_t* arg2 @ 0xc)" at 0x004101C0; radare2 recovers "fcn.004101c0 (int32_t arg_24h, int32_t arg_2ch);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004101C0 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t DefineHumanPlayerWeaponCycle(int32_t param_1, int32_t* param_2);.
